current noun

of a river or the sea

also current of a river, against the current, with the current, upstream, downstream, strong current

classical

Caes. BG 7.58: secundō flūmine, with the current
Caes. BG 7.60: adversō flūmine, against the current
Traupman 203: current (in the sense of “the flow”), flūmen
Traupman 299

flūmen, flūminis n.

noun, third declension; in this sense in set phrases

the stream, the current (flowing water)

Properly “a flowing” (Lewis & Short), and so the current itself: secundō flūmine, with the current, downstream; adversō flūmine, against it, upstream. The force of the current is vīs flūminis (Caes. BG 4.15; Traupman 203).

Other words

  • aestus, aestūs m. — a current at sea; the tide

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.23: et ventum et aestum ūnō tempore … secundum

    See tide.

  • rapiditās, rapiditātis f. — the speed of a current

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Caes. BG 4.17: propter lātitūdinem, rapiditātem altitūdinemque flūminis

    Rare: Caesar’s word for the rush of the Rhine (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • nōn aliter quam quī adversō vix flūmine lembum rēmigiīs subigit, sī bracchia forte remīsit, atque illum in praeceps prōnō rapit alveus amnī

    just like a man who can barely row his boat against the current: if he happens to slacken his arms, the channel sweeps it headlong downstreamVerg. G. 1.201–203

  • adversō flūmine

    against the currentTraupman 299

  • secundō flūmine

    with the currentTraupman 299

See also river, stream, tide, sea.
